3
Vectors P and Q are drawn to scale.
P
Q
Which diagram represents the vector (P – Q)?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice the given vectors: $P$ is short and points up-right while $Q$ is longer and points down-right.
Recall that $P - Q = P + (-Q)$, so first imagine $Q$ reversed to point up-left with the same long length.
Add $P$ to that reversed $Q$: the horizontal result must point left and the vertical result must point strongly up, so look for a long up-left arrow.
walkthrough: Identify the components: $P$ has a small rightward $x$-component and a small upward $y$-component, while $Q$ has a large rightward $x$-component and a large downward $y$-component.
Use the subtraction rule $P - Q = P + (-Q)$. The vector $-Q$ has the same length as $Q$ but opposite direction, so it points up-left with large leftward and large upward components.
Add components: for $x$, small right from $P$ plus large left from $-Q$ gives a net leftward component. For $y$, small up from $P$ plus large up from $-Q$ gives a net large upward component.
Therefore $P - Q$ must be longer than $P$, point to the left, and point steeply upward.
Option A points down-right and option D points right, so neither has the required upward-left direction. Option B points left but is almost horizontal with no large upward part.
Only the long arrow pointing steeply up and slightly left satisfies both the direction and the length. This is option C.

A.explanation: This points down and to the right, which is the direction of $Q - P$, the opposite of the required vector.

B.explanation: This points to the left and is almost horizontal, but $P - Q$ must have a large upward component from subtracting $Q$.

C.explanation: This points up and slightly to the left with large length, matching $P$ plus the reversed long $Q$ vector.

D.explanation: This points to the right and is almost horizontal, which is close to the direction of $P + Q$, not $P - Q$.
